gloss: to go out, to leave, to appear

definitions.gloss: to go out, to leave, to exit
definitions.explanation: To move from inside to outside a place. The opposite of {入|はい}る (hairu).
For something to become visible or available, such as results or products.
To be present at meetings, events, or competitions.

examples.english: I leave the house at 8 o'clock.
examples.notes: Note: を particle for leaving a place

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}に{出|で}てください。

examples.notes: Sense 1: から marks the origin

examples.japanese: {授業|じゅぎょう}に{出|で}なければなりません。
{試合|しあい}に{出|で}たいです。
examples.english: I want to participate in the match.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}から{出|で}るとき、{気|き}をつけてください。
examples.english: Please be careful when getting off the train.

examples.japanese: {熱|ねつ}が{出|で}たので、{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}みました。
examples.english: I got a fever, so I was absent from school.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{日曜日|にちようび}の{会|かい}に{出|で}ています。
examples.english: I attend the meeting every Sunday.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}を{出|で}てから、この{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}いています。
examples.english: Since graduating from university, I've been working at this company.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{本|ほん}が{出|で}たので、{買|か}いに{行|い}きました。
examples.english: A new book came out, so I went to buy it.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}のパーティーに{出|で}る{予定|よてい}ですが、{時間|じかん}があるかどうか{分|わ}かりません。
examples.english: I plan to attend next month's party, but I don't know if I'll have time.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pair: {出|だ}す (transitive). Pattern: Xを{出|で}る (leave X) / Xに{出|で}る (attend X).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {出|で}ている = 'has left' or 'is out.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{家|いえ}を{出|で}る (leave home - uses を)
・{会議|かいぎ}に{出|で}る (attend a meeting - uses に)
・{結果|けっか}が{出|で}る (results come out)
・{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}る (answer the phone)

PAIR: {出|だ}す (transitive) - {本|ほん}を{出|だ}した (took out the book). Opposite: {入|はい}る (to enter).
